etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From English vitamin or German Vitamin.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Borrowed from English bench.
Doublet of バンク.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
⟨mo₂to₂⟩ → /moto/
From Old Japanese. Cited to the Kojiki of 712 CE. From Proto-Japonic *mətə. Doublet of 下(もと) (moto, “base, basis”). Cognate with Okinawan 元 (mutu).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: The 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 勝(か)つ (katsu, “to win”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
The 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 好(す)く (suku, “to like, to be fond of, to enjoy, to feel love for”).
First cited to the late 900s in the 宇津保物語 (Utsubo Monogatari).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Old Japanese, ultimately from Proto-Japonic *yanto.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From the 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 流(なが)れる (nagareru, “to flow”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/fumite/ → /fũnde/ → /fude/
Shift in pronunciation from fumite below, caused by a regular shift where medial み (mi) causes nasalization of the preceding vowel and voicing of the following consonant, with the nasalization reverting in some cases. Now the most common pronunciation in modern Japanese.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/fumite/ → /fũnde/ → /funde/
Shift in pronunciation from fumite below, caused by a regular shift where medial み (mi) causes nasalization of the preceding vowel and voicing of the following consonant. Listed with this reading in the 観智院 (Kanchi-in) edition of the 11th- or 12th-century 類聚名義抄 (Ruiju Myōgishō) dictionary.
Superseded by the fude reading above in modern Japanese.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Compound of 文 (fumi, “writing”) + 手 (te, “hand”). Appears with this reading in the Man'yōshū, circa 759.
Superseded by the fude reading above in modern Japanese.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/pitu/ → /fitu/ → /hitu/
From Middle Chinese 筆 /笔 (pit, “writing brush”). Compare modern Hakka and Min Nan pit, Mandarin bǐ.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From the 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 続(つづ)く (tsuzuku, “to continue”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
⟨mame₂⟩ → /mame/
From Old Japanese, in turn from Proto-Japonic *mamay.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/wepu/ → /wefu/ → /jefu/ → */jewu/ → */jowu/ → /jou/
Shift from classical verb 酔ふ (efu → eu), possibly parsed as jefu, itself from Old Japanese 酔ふ (wepu → wefu → eu).
Compare the development of 葉 (efu → yō, “leaf”, on-yomi or Chinese-derived reading).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Regular development of wepu. In the colloquial language, wepu developed into you, so eu is now only used in reading ancient texts.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: The 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 間(ま)違(ちが)う (machigau, “to make a mistake”).
